description: Pass rules of D34 step 6: how the georegistration weighs GPS against the compass (three switches in crowd3d.params.Params: gps_span_model_side, compass_other, yaw_arbitration; findings of the code review, which did not measure them on real models). The switches were measured by offline replay (benchmark.py rescore --replay) of the recorded D31 runs of the dev split, and the defaults chosen there by a rule written down beforehand (dev_rule, dev_outcome). This file states what is then run ONCE on the held-out split, from the commit that adds this file, and how it is judged (held_out). It was written after the dev replays and before any replay of the held-out split; no number of the held-out split under any switch was looked at before. The rules are judged by compare --criteria d34-v1 --noise-factor 0 (A and B score the same SfM artefacts, so run-to-run noise does not enter a difference); the checks read the result files and benchmark.py georeg's JSON and are judged outside compare. docs/BENCHMARK.md section 6.13.

baseline.B: The arm under test (held_out.nominated), the same command with its own --replay config; without a nominated arm there is no B and compare is run as A against the plain rescore (rescore --testset commons-ten-v1 --from eval/results/commons-ten-v1/d31-<split>.json --name d34-plain-<split> --restylize --reference-cache <scratch>/d31/fresh/refs/commons-ten-v1), which the control must reproduce. Dev runs: commit 65781fd. Held-out runs: the commit that adds this file. No COLMAP runs: a replay reads the kept sparse models of d31-dev / d31-test (their work dirs, never written to).

decisions: D34 (owner, 2026-11-10): implement the code review's recommendations. The lead's brief for this step: each of the three georegistration fixes behind its own switch, measured on recorded runs without new SfM, defaults by evidence; a fix that does not help on dev stays off; held-out numbers are looked at once, after this file is committed, and nothing is tuned after them.

What a replay shows: the georegistration, the camera checks, the QA gate's verdict and the supersede rule of every stored model, made again from its job's kept sparse model. What it cannot show: the candidate a job would have chosen among its mapping attempts, the retries a suspicious candidate triggers, and the jobs later uploads would have queued had an earlier model been published or not. A default changed on replay evidence therefore still needs a fresh run before the next result is recorded under it.
Settings.facing_away_warns_other_refs (the fourth switch) changes which photos are accepted and cannot be replayed; it is off and outside this file.

Defaults in code change only after a held-out PASS: until then the switches are applied through the replay configs, so the product's output is unchanged whatever the held-out run shows. A held-out FAIL or INSUFFICIENT leaves every default off (the code and the switches stay).

dev_rule.written: 2026-11-11, in the step's working notes, before any arm's full result; committed with docs/BENCHMARK.md 6.13 in 65781fd, before the dev runs reported here were made from that commit. Not blind: an exploratory replay on the uncommitted code had been looked at (per-model scale and yaw before the rule was written; the arms' full results after), and one code change followed it (readings the yaw arbitration overruled no longer flag a camera or fail the model at the QA gate).
dev_rule.compared_with: the control arm off, on the dev split
dev_rule.numbers: benchmark.py georeg --split dev: errors over the distinct checked models (published, georegistered, at least 3 unflagged cameras with a verified, oriented reference pose); counts are the split aggregate (the median of each building's two repeats, summed over buildings)
helps_any_of: checked models with the scale off by more than 35 %: at least 2 fewer, or RMS |ln scale| at least 5 % lower
yaw RMS at least 5 % lower, or checked models with the yaw off by more than 15 deg: at least 2 fewer
photo_pose_wrong at least 2 lower with photo_pose_correct not lower
photo_pose_correct at least 2 higher with photo_pose_wrong not higher
no_harm_all_of: models_published not lower by more than 1
photo_pose_determined not lower by more than 1 %
photo_pose_correct not lower by more than 1
shown poses beyond their own 2 sigma (photo_pose_gt_determined - photo_pose_within_uncertainty) not higher by more than 1
wrong_face_models_published not higher; wrong_face_cameras_shown not higher
each of calib_yaw_cover2, calib_scale_cover2, calib_xy_cover2, calib_tilt_cover2 not lower by more than 0.02
checked models with the scale off by more than 35 % not higher by more than 1; with the yaw off by more than 15 deg not higher by more than 1
dev_rule.choice: an arm's switches may become defaults only if it helps and does no harm; among qualifying arms the one with the fewest switches, unless a larger one is better again by one of the helps measures; with no qualifying arm every switch stays off and no switched-on arm is run on the held-out split

held_out.verdict: PASS when every rule and every check passes; FAIL when one fails; INSUFFICIENT when none fails and one lacks data. PASS: the nominated arm's switches become the defaults (RECON_OUTPUT_VERSION 3). FAIL or INSUFFICIENT: every default stays off.

rules.why: Hard guard: no published model on the wrong face, on every building and every repeat of B.
The wrong rate among shown poses with a reference pose, pooled and on every building: not worse beyond sampling noise (95 % Newcombe interval of the difference).
Judged by the checks (helps / no harm).
The raw count, next to the rate.
The denominator of the wrong rate.
Poses shown: judged by check no_harm.
Scale error of the checked models, reported.

checks.require: on the held-out split the control arm (off) equals the plain rescore from the same commit
checks.how: d34-off-test against d34-plain-test: every metric of every repeat of every building equal, except the wall-clock, CPU and peak-memory metrics of the stylize step (style_*_s, struct_*_s, *_rss_mb, *cpu*); every calibration row equal; and in the control's replay blocks transform_changed 0, level_changed and published_changed empty. A model left as recorded is listed with its reason and is not a failure: it is scored as recorded in both. On dev: 238 of 238 models replayed, none moved, every metric and calibration row equal.
checks.why: A replay that does not reproduce the recorded run with the recorded parameters measures nothing.

checks.require: the nominated arm against the control on the held-out split: at least one of dev_rule.helps_any_of
checks.how: benchmark.py georeg d34-off-test d34-<arm>-test --split test --json: overall.errors (scale_off, scale_rms_ln, yaw_rms_deg, yaw_off) and overall.counts (photo_pose_correct, photo_pose_wrong), the same arithmetic as on dev. No value on either side of a measure (no checked model): that measure cannot be met.
checks.why: A default that changes every model's georegistration must show its benefit out of sample.

checks.require: the nominated arm against the control on the held-out split: all of dev_rule.no_harm_all_of
checks.how: the same georeg JSON: overall.counts and overall.errors. A coverage with no checked model on either side is not judged and is named; the check is INSUFFICIENT when none of the four coverages can be judged.
checks.why: The switches must not publish fewer models, show fewer or worse poses, or loosen the stated ranges.

checks.require: style_registration_wrong, style_qa_failed, struct_incorrect and struct_qa_failed of the nominated arm not above the control's on any building and repeat of the held-out split
checks.how: the two result files, every repeat's metrics; a value missing on both sides counts as equal.
checks.why: Replayed models are stylized again: a georegistration that makes the footprint snap go wrong is harm.

checks.require: only the arms listed in held_out.run_once exist for the held-out split
checks.how: the result files committed under eval/results/commons-ten-v1/d34-regeo/.
checks.why: Every held-out run is kept and reported; an arm that was not nominated is not looked at there.
